record.title: Katz's conjectural description of the generic Galois group
record.statement: Let ${\mathcal M}=(M,\nabla)$ be a differential module over $\mathbb Q(x)$, let $\operatorname{Gal}({\mathcal M})$ be its generic Galois group, and let $\psi_p$ denote the $p$-curvature for almost all primes $p$. **Katz's conjectural description of the generic Galois group.** The Lie algebra of $\operatorname{Gal}({\mathcal M})$ is the smallest algebraic Lie subalgebra of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q(x)}(M)$ whose reduction modulo $p$ contains $\psi_p$ for almost all $p$. This is presented as an arithmetic description equivalent to Grothendieck's conjecture on $p$-curvatures and would give a conjectural positive answer to the direct problem in differential Galois theory; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Lucia Di Vizio and Charlotte Hardouin, “Intrinsic approach to Galois theory of q-difference equations, with the preface to Part 4 "The Galois D-groupoid of a q-difference system'' by Anne Granier”, arXiv:1002.4839 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.4839

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2010).

record.title: Dense fixed-subgraph conjecture for the final H-free process
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a strictly $2$-balanced graph, and let $d_2(H)$ denote its $2$-density. Let $F$ be a fixed non-empty graph satisfying

$$
m(F)>d_2(H).
$$

**Dense fixed-subgraph conjecture.** With high probability, the final graph of the $H$-free process contains no copy of $F$.
This strengthens the proved result for graphs whose number of vertices may grow moderately with $n$, and is motivated by the fact that the known bound for the maximum density of fixed graphs appearing in the process is best possible up to constants. The statement is presented as a belief in the source, and no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Lutz Warnke, “Dense subgraphs in the H-free process”, arXiv:1003.0220 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.0220

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2010).

record.title: General Hodge conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme, let $l\ge1$ and $p\ge0$, and define the coniveau filtration by

$$
F^p_aH^l(X,\mathbb Q)=\bigcup_{\operatorname{codim}_X(Y)\ge p}\ker\bigl(H^l(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^l(X-Y,\mathbb Q)\bigr).
$$

Here $F^pH^l(X,\mathbb C)$ is the Hodge filtration. **General Hodge conjecture.** $F^p_aH^l(X,\mathbb Q)$ is the largest sub-Hodge structure of

$$
F^pH^l(X,\mathbb C)\cap H^l(X,\mathbb Q).
$$

The source presents this as the general Hodge conjecture and gives no resolution status for the asserted statement.
record.source_name: Amalendu Krishna, “A cdh approach to zero-cycles on singular varieties”, arXiv:1003.0264 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.0264

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2010). “This conjecture is open till date though it has been proven for surfaces which are not of general type .”

record.title: TBR adjacency implies BME adjacency
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the space of trees on $n$ leaves. For $T,T'\in\mathcal{T}_n$, let $d_{TBR}(T,T')$ denote the minimum number of tree-bisection-regrafting moves needed to transform $T$ to $T'$. Let $d_{BME}(T,T')=1$ when the corresponding vertices $\mathbf{w}^T$ and $\mathbf{w}^{T'}$ are joined by an edge in the balanced minimum evolution polytope $\mathcal{P}_n$. **TBR adjacency conjecture.** If $T,T'\in\mathcal{T}_n$, then

$$
d_{TBR}(T,T')=1
$$

implies

$$
d_{BME}(T,T')=1.
$$

Nearest-neighbor interchange adjacency implies subtree-prune-regraft adjacency, and subtree-prune-regraft adjacency is known to imply BME adjacency. The paper reports no examples showing that TBR adjacency fails to imply BME adjacency, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: David C. Haws, Terrell Hodge and Ruriko Yoshida, “Optimality of the Neighbor Joining Algorithm and Faces of the Balanced Minimum Evolution Polytope”, arXiv:1004.2073 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.2073

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2010).

record.title: The smallest eigenvalue of a circulant B-spline matrix
record.statement:
Let $C_m^d$ be the circulant associated with the degree-$d$ B-spline collocation matrix, with Toeplitz symbol coefficients $t_0^d,\ldots,t_r^d$, and let $\lambda_\mu(C_m^d)$ denote its smallest eigenvalue. **The smallest-eigenvalue conjecture.** The circulant $C_m^d$ is always positive definite, and the index $\mu$ of its smallest eigenvalue is always the integer nearest to $m/2$; explicitly, 

$$
\lambda_{\mu}(C_m^d)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\lambda_{(m\pm1)/2}(C_m^d)=t_0^d+2\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^jt_j^d\cos\left(\frac{\pi j}{m}\right),&m\text{ odd},\\[4pt]\displaystyle\lambda_{m/2}(C_m^d)=t_0^d+2\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^jt_j^d,&m\text{ even.}\end{cases}
$$

The statement is presented as a conjecture based on extensive numerical testing; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Vedran Novakovic, Sanja Singer and Sasa Singer, “Estimates for the Spectral Condition Number of Cardinal B-Spline Collocation Matrices (Long version)”, arXiv:1004.4014 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.4014

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2010). “The conjecture was disproved by Rong--Qing Jia in 1988.”

record.title: NP-completeness conjecture for generalized $k_1$-connectivity
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $k_1\geq 3$ be fixed. For each $k_1$-subset $S$ of $V(G)$, let $\kappa(S)$ be the maximum number of internally disjoint trees connecting $S$, and define

$$
\kappa_{k_1}(G)=\min\{\kappa(S): S\subseteq V(G),\ |S|=k_1\}.
$$

Let $k$ be an integer satisfying

$$
2\leq k\leq n-1.
$$

**The generalized-connectivity NP-completeness conjecture.** Given $G$ and $k$, deciding whether

$$
\kappa_{k_1}(G)\geq k
$$

is NP-complete. For fixed $k_1$ and fixed $k$, the corresponding decision problems are described as polynomial-time solvable, whereas the variable-$k$ complexity remains unknown, including the case $k_1=3$.
record.source_name: Shasha Li and Xueliang Li, “Hardness results on generalized connectivity”, arXiv:1005.0488 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.0488

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2010).

record.title: The quotient monotonicity conjecture for totally skew embeddings
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let a finite group $\Gamma$ act freely on $M$. Let $N(M)$ denote the smallest dimension in which $M$ admits a totally skew embedding.

**Quotient monotonicity conjecture.** One should have

$$
N(M)\leq N(M/\Gamma),
$$

and, in particular,

$$
N(S^n)\leq N(\mathbb{R}P^n).
$$

The conjecture expresses the expectation that a totally skew immersion obtained by composing an embedding of the quotient with the covering map can be perturbed to a totally skew embedding of the covering manifold. It is listed among the paper's open problems.
record.source_name: Djordje Baralic, Branislav Prvulovic, Gordana Stojanovic, Sinisa Vrecica and Rade Zivaljevic, “Topological obstructions to totally skew embeddings”, arXiv:1005.3709 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.3709

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2010). “This and a sample of other open problems and conjectures can be found in the final section of the paper where we also offer a brief outlook to future research.”

record.title: The product lower-bound conjecture for totally skew embeddings
record.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be manifolds, and let $N(X)$ and $N(Y)$ denote the smallest dimensions in which they admit totally skew embeddings.

**Product lower-bound conjecture.** The invariant should satisfy

$$
N(X\times Y)\geq N(X)+N(Y)-1.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by comparing the bundle-splitting inequalities for $X$, $Y$, and $X\times Y$. If true, together with the known lower bound $N(\mathbb{R}^n)\geq 3n$ when $n$ is a power of $2$, it would imply further lower bounds for products and Euclidean spaces. It is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Djordje Baralic, Branislav Prvulovic, Gordana Stojanovic, Sinisa Vrecica and Rade Zivaljevic, “Topological obstructions to totally skew embeddings”, arXiv:1005.3709 (2010).

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2010). “This and a sample of other open problems and conjectures can be found in the final section of the paper where we also offer a brief outlook to future research.”

record.title: The simplex conjecture for random simplex volumes
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $T^d$ be a $d$-dimensional simplex, let $p\geqslant 1$, and let $n\geqslant d+1$. Write $\mathbb{E}^p_*(K)$ and $\mathbb{E}^p_n(K)$ for the random-simplex volume functionals defined in the paper. **Simplex conjecture.** One has

$$
\mathbb{E}^p_*(K)\leqslant\mathbb{E}^p_*(T^d)\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mathbb{E}^p_n(K)\leqslant\mathbb{E}^p_n(T^d),
$$

with equality if and only if $K$ is a simplex. This is presented as the most general conjecture governing the maximum of the random-simplex functionals; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Gergely Ambrus and Károly J. Böröczky, “Stability results for the volume of random simplices”, arXiv:1005.5024 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.5024

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2010). “There are various equivalent formulations of this major open problem; for thorough surveys, consult the papers V.D. Milman and A. Pajor , and A.A. Giannopoulos and V.D. Milman for some later results.”

record.title: Zero-spacing preservation under a unit difference
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}_n$ denote the real polynomials of degree $n$ with only real zeros, and let $\mu(p)$ be the minimum spacing between neighboring zeros. For $p$, define $g(x)=p(x+1)-p(x)$. **Zero-spacing conjecture.** If $p(x)\in\mathcal{L}\text{-}\mathcal{P}_n$, $n\ge 2$, and $\mu(p)\ge d\ge 1$, then $\mu(g)\ge d$. This would extend the known monotonicity of mesh under differentiation to a discrete difference operator; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: George Csordas and Matthew Chasse, “Discrete analogues of the Laguerre inequalities and a conjecture of I. Krasikov”, arXiv:1005.5186 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.5186

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2010).

record.title: Tightness conjecture for the centered maximum of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field
record.statement:
Let $V_N=([0,N]\cap\mathbb{Z})^2$ and let $\{X_z^N\}_{z\in V_N}$ be the zero-mean discrete two-dimensional Gaussian free field on $V_N$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Define

$$
X_N^*=\max_{z\in V_N}X_z^N,\qquad Y_N:=X_N^*-E X_N^*.
$$

**Tightness conjecture.** The sequence of random variables $\{Y_N\}_{N\geq 1}$ is tight.

The paper proves tightness along a dense deterministic subsequence, while tightness for the full sequence remains open. The conjecture concerns the fluctuations of the maximum after centering by its mean, beyond the established first-order asymptotics $X_N^*/\log N\to 2\sqrt{2/\pi}$.
record.source_name: Erwin Bolthausen, Jean-Dominique Deuschel and Ofer Zeitouni, “Recursions and tightness for the maximum of the discrete, two dimensional Gaussian Free Field”, arXiv:1005.5417 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.5417

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2010).

record.title: Jackson and Ordaz's connectivity and independence conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
For a digraph $G$, let $\kappa(G)$ be the minimum size of a vertex set whose deletion leaves a digraph that is not strongly connected or is a single vertex. Let $\alpha_2(G)$ be the maximum size of a vertex set inducing no cycle of length $2$.

**Jackson and Ordaz's conjecture.** If

$$
\kappa(G)\geq \alpha_2(G)+1,
$$

then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle.

The conjecture is presented as a weaker version of the possible condition $\kappa(G)\geq\alpha_2(G)\geq4$, and is described as still wide open. A stronger pancyclic conclusion was also mentioned in the surrounding context.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “A survey on Hamilton cycles in directed graphs”, arXiv:1006.0590 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.0590

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2010). “It is even an open problem whether the conditions imply the existence of a cycle through any pair of given vertices (see ).”

record.title: Kelly, Kühn and Osthus's short-cycle conjecture for oriented graphs
record.statement:
Let $\ell\geq4$ be a positive integer, and let $k$ be the smallest integer greater than $2$ that does not divide $\ell$. Let $\delta^0(G)$ denote the minimum semidegree of an oriented graph $G$.

**Kelly, Kühn and Osthus's conjecture.** There exists an integer $n_0=n_0(\ell)$ such that every oriented graph $G$ on $n\geq n_0$ vertices with

$$
\delta^0(G)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor+1
$$

contains an $\ell$-cycle.

The conjecture refines known minimum-semidegree thresholds for forcing cycles of prescribed lengths. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “A survey on Hamilton cycles in directed graphs”, arXiv:1006.0590 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.0590

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2010). “It is even an open problem whether the conditions imply the existence of a cycle through any pair of given vertices (see ).”

record.title: Frieze–Krivelevich Hamilton decomposition conjecture for random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph and let $\delta(G_{n,p})$ denote its minimum degree. **Frieze–Krivelevich conjecture.** For any $p$, with high probability, $G_{n,p}$ contains

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{\delta(G_{n,p})}{2}\right\rfloor
$$

edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This conjecture strengthens the fixed-density Hamilton-decomposition results for random graphs. It was proved in the form stated in the source by Bollobás and subsequently generalized by Bollobás and Frieze.
record.source_name: Fiachra Knox, Daniela Kühn and Deryk Osthus, “Approximate Hamilton Decompositions of Random Graphs”, arXiv:1006.1268 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.1268

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2010).

record.title: King and Pelsmajer's bounded-exception domination conjecture for plane triangulations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex plane triangulation, and let $t$ be a fixed nonnegative integer. A vertex has **degree other than $6$** when its degree in $G$ is not equal to $6$. A **dominating set** is a set of vertices such that every vertex is either in the set or adjacent to a vertex in the set.

**King and Pelsmajer's conjecture.** For any constant $t$, there exists $n_t$ such that every $n$-vertex plane triangulation with $n>n_t$ and at most $t$ vertices of degree other than $6$ has a dominating set of size at most $n/4$.

This extends the previously studied maximum-degree-at-most-$6$ case to triangulations with only a bounded number of exceptional-degree vertices. The paper states this as a conjecture and subsequently proves a stronger bound under the same bounded-exception hypothesis.
record.source_name: Hong Liu and Michael J. Pelsmajer, “Dominating Sets in Triangulations on Surfaces”, arXiv:1006.1879 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.1879

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2010); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Continuous $d$-step Conjecture for central-path curvature
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda(n,d)$ denote the largest total curvature of a central path over polytopes defined by $n$ inequalities in dimension $d$ and over all linear objectives.

**Continuous $d$-step Conjecture.** The function $\Lambda(2d,d)$ grows linearly in its input; that is,

$$
\Lambda(2d,d) \in O(d).
$$

The source states that this conjecture is equivalent to the Continuous Hirsch Conjecture. The supplied material gives no resolution of either conjecture.
record.source_name: Edward D. Kim, “Geometric Combinatorics of Transportation Polytopes and the Behavior of the Simplex Method”, arXiv:1006.2416 (2010).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2010). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0907.1186](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1186).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2416

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2010).

record.title: Hähnle's linear-in-dimension Hirsch conjecture
record.statement: Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional polytope with $n$ facets, and let its diameter be the maximum length of a shortest edge path between two vertices of $P$. **Hähnle's conjecture.** The diameter of every $d$-polytope with $n$ facets is bounded above by $dn$. This is presented as a more explicit version of the polynomial Hirsch conjecture; the source says that the underlying diameter problem remains largely open and attributes this formulation to N. Hähnle.
record.source_name: Francisco Santos, “A counterexample to the Hirsch conjecture”, arXiv:1006.2814 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2814

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2010).

record.title: Hähnle's sharpened linear Hirsch conjecture
record.statement: Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional polytope with $n$ facets, and let its diameter be the maximum length of a shortest edge path between two vertices of $P$. **Hähnle's sharpened conjecture.** The diameter of every $d$-polytope with $n$ facets is bounded above by $d(n-d)$. The source states that, using an earlier remark, this formulation is almost equivalent to the bound $dn$; the question of general diameter bounds remains open.
record.source_name: Francisco Santos, “A counterexample to the Hirsch conjecture”, arXiv:1006.2814 (2011).

record.title: The discrete-torus path-length conjecture
record.statement: Let $C_3^n$ be the $n$-dimensional discrete torus, and let $G$ be a subgraph of $C_3^n$ with minimum degree at least $d$. **The discrete-torus path-length conjecture.** $G$ must contain a path of length at least $3^{\frac{d}{2}}-1$. The surrounding discussion notes that the bound is not expected from the preceding method and asks what the correct lower bound should be; the paper subsequently proves the weaker bound $2^{\frac{d}{4}}$.
record.source_name: Eoin Long, “Long paths and cycles in subgraphs of the cube”, arXiv:1006.3049 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3049

record.title: Montassier et al.'s bounded-degree forest decomposition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $d$ be positive integers, and let $G$ be a graph. Write $\Upsilon_f(G)$ for the fractional arboricity of $G$, defined by

$$
\Upsilon_f(G)=\max_{H\subseteq G}\frac{|E(H)|}{|V(H)|-1}.
$$

**Montassier et al.'s conjecture.** If

$$
\Upsilon_f(G)\leq k+\frac{d}{k+d+1},
$$

then $E(G)$ can be decomposed into $k+1$ forests, one of which has maximum degree at most $d$.

This conjecture generalizes the known decompositions of graphs with fractional arboricity at most $\tfrac{4}{3}$ or $\tfrac{3}{2}$. It is open for $k\geq 2$ or $d\geq 7$.
record.source_name: Tomas Kaiser, Mickael Montassier and Andre Raspaud, “Covering a graph by forests and a matching”, arXiv:1007.0316 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0316

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2010). “For $k \geq 2$ or $d\geq 7$, the conjecture is open.”

record.title: Wenger's conjecture on the chromatic number of squares of planar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and let $G^2$ denote its square, in which two vertices are adjacent whenever their distance in $G$ is at most $2$. **Wenger's conjecture.**

$$
\chi(G^2)\leq 7 \quad\text{when } \Delta=3,
$$

$$
\chi(G^2)\leq \Delta+5 \quad\text{when } 4\leq \Delta\leq 7,
$$

$$
\chi(G^2)\leq \frac{3\Delta}{2}+1 \quad\text{when } \Delta\geq 8.
$$

This conjecture concerns upper bounds for coloring the square of a planar graph, a problem closely related to injective coloring and other graph-labeling questions. The supplied material does not establish whether all three bounds are known, so its resolution status remains open.
record.source_name: Daniel W. Cranston, Seog-Jin Kim and Gexin Yu, “Injective colorings of sparse graphs”, arXiv:1007.0786 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0786

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2010).

record.title: Noncommuting one-parameter subgroups conjecture for continuous interval exchange actions
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the topological group of continuous interval exchange actions, and let $F=\{f_t\}$ and $G=\{g_s\}$ be one-parameter subgroups of $\mathcal{E}$. **Noncommuting one-parameter subgroups conjecture.** If $F$ and $G$ do not commute, then the group $\langle F,G\rangle$ has elements that are not contained in any one-parameter subgroup of $\mathcal{E}$. The commuting case is described by simultaneous conjugacy to subgroups of a common standard torus action; the conjecture asserts that noncommuting one-parameter subgroups exhibit fundamentally different behavior. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.
record.source_name: Christopher F. Novak, “Continuous Interval Exchange Actions”, arXiv:1007.1221 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.1221

record.title: Kohnen–Mason conjecture on integral generalized modular forms
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer. A **generalized modular form** $f$ for $Gamma_0(N)$ has a Fourier expansion at $infty$ defined over $\mathbf{Z}$, and its smallest nonzero Fourier coefficient is normalized to be $1$.

**Kohnen–Mason conjecture.** Under these conditions, $f$ is a classical modular form.

The conjecture concerns when integrality and a normalization condition force a generalized modular form to have a classical transformation character. Its resolution is not stated in the source.
record.source_name: L J P Kilford and Wissam Raji, “On generalized modular forms supported on cuspidal and elliptic points”, arXiv:1007.5257 (2010).

record.title: Semisimplicity conjecture for convolution complexes
record.statement:
Let $D$, $V$, and $V'$ be as above, and let $K_1\cdot K_2\cdot\ldots\cdot K_m$ be a convolution complex in

$$
\mathscr D^-_{\mathbf G}(\mathbf E_{\Omega}(D,V,V')),
$$

where each $K_a$ is either $\mathscr E^{(n),\Omega}_{\bullet}$ or $\mathscr F^{(n),\Omega}_{\bullet}$. **Semisimplicity conjecture.** The complexes $K_1\cdot K_2\cdot\ldots\cdot K_m$ are bounded and semisimple.

This conjecture is needed to construct the algebra of classes of simple perverse sheaves arising as direct summands of these complexes and to establish the geometric realization of the modified quantum algebra. The source explicitly assumes it for the remainder of the section; no resolution status is supplied here.

record.title: The exponential properly coloured path or cycle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-coloured graph, and let $delta^c(G)$ denote its minimum colour degree. A **properly coloured (p.c.) path or cycle** is one whose consecutive edges have distinct colours. **Exponential path-cycle conjecture.** For integers $k ge 3$, every edge-coloured graph $G$ with

$$
delta^c(G) ge k-1
$$

contains a p.c. path of length $k2^{delta^c(G)-k+2}-2$ or a p.c. cycle of length at least $k$. The bound would match the construction giving p.c. paths of length $k2^{delta^c(G)-k+2}-2$ and p.c. cycles of length $k-1$, so the conjecture would make the known exponential result best possible.
record.source_name: Allan Lo, “A Dirac type condition for properly coloured paths and cycles”, arXiv:1008.3242 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3242

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2010).

record.title: The properly coloured Hamiltonian cycle or long path conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-coloured graph, and let $delta^c(G)$ denote its minimum colour degree. A **properly coloured (p.c.) path or cycle** is one whose consecutive edges have distinct colours; a p.c. Hamiltonian cycle is a p.c. cycle containing every vertex of $G$. **Long path conjecture.** Every edge-coloured graph $G$ contains a p.c. Hamiltonian cycle or a p.c. path of length

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{3delta^c(G)}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by a connected construction with minimum colour degree $d$ whose longest p.c. path has length $\lfloor 3d/2\rfloor$; it asserts that this example is best possible unless a p.c. Hamiltonian cycle exists.
record.source_name: Allan Lo, “A Dirac type condition for properly coloured paths and cycles”, arXiv:1008.3242 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3242

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2010).

record.title: Transitivity of arrows between impartial misère-game positions
record.statement: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ be impartial positions. An arrow $\delta\to\varepsilon$ exists when Left moving second can win $\varepsilon+\delta^{\circ}$, or under a similar criterion. **Transitivity conjecture.** If arrows $\alpha\to\beta$ and $\beta\to\gamma$ exist, then an arrow $\alpha\to\gamma$ exists. The conjecture would establish transitivity of the arrow relation on impartial positions and could help determine whether these positions form a Joyal-style category under a suitable sum and negative; the paper gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Meghan Rose Allen, “An Investigation of Partizan Misere Games”, arXiv:1008.4109 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.4109

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2010).

record.title: Kunita's exchange conjecture for purely nondeterministic hidden Markov models
record.statement:
Let $(X_k,Y_k)_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a stationary hidden Markov model with hidden state space $E$ and observation space $F$. The hidden process is **purely nondeterministic** if

$$
\mathbf{E}\big[|\mathbf{P}[X_n\in A|X_0]-\mu(A) |\big]
 \xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0
$$

for every $A\in\mathcal{B}(E)$, where $\mu$ is the invariant distribution of $X_0$. The observations are **nondegenerate** if there exist a $\sigma$-finite reference measure $\varphi$ on $F$ and a strictly positive measurable function $g:E\times F\to]0,\infty[$ such that

$$
\Phi(x,A) = \int \mathbf{1}_A(y)\\,g(x,y)\\,\varphi(dy)
$$

for all $x\in E$ and $A\in\mathcal{B}(F)$. The exchange identity is the equality between the intersection and supremum of the relevant sigma-fields, denoted by $$ in the source.

**Kunita's exchange conjecture.** If the hidden process is purely nondeterministic and the observations are nondegenerate, then $$ holds true.

This conjecture would extend the known result from absolutely regular hidden processes to purely nondeterministic ones. The source states that it was conjectured in the cited work and provides no resolution here.

record.title: Eigenvalue-crossing conjecture for non-planar transfer matrices
record.statement: Consider a family $G_{n,L}$ of non-planar connected graphs as above. Let $Q_\ell$ be the smallest $Q>0$ for which the transfer matrix $\widetilde{\sf T}_{L,\ell,(\ell)}$ for the fully symmetric representation $(\ell)$ of $\ell$ marked blocks has at least two dominant eigenvalues, or set $Q_\ell=\infty$ if none exists. For $Q\in(0,Q_\ell)$, let $\lambda_\ell$ be the unique dominant eigenvalue. **Eigenvalue-crossing conjecture.** One has $Q_0<Q_1<Q_2<\cdots$; each $\lambda_\ell$ is real; the equation $|\lambda_\ell|=|\lambda_{\ell'}|$ has at most one solution for $0<Q<\min(Q_\ell,Q_{\ell'})$; and, if a solution exists, it is $Q=\ell+\ell'-1$. The source reports validation for generalized Petersen graphs with $L=k+1$ and $k\leq7$.
record.source_name: Jesper L. Jacobsen and Jesus Salas, “Is the five-flow conjecture almost false?”, arXiv:1009.4062 (2013).

record.title: Conforti–Johnson's Petersen-minor T-join min-max conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $T$ be the set of its odd-degree vertices. A **$T$-join** is a subgraph whose odd-degree vertices are precisely the vertices in $T$, and a **$T$-cut** is a cut $(A,B)$ such that $|T\cap A|$ is odd. **Conforti–Johnson's Petersen-minor T-join min-max conjecture.** If $G$ has no Petersen minor, then the maximum number of edge-disjoint $T$-joins equals the size of the smallest $T$-cut. The paper states that this conjecture would follow from Seymour's Petersen-minor edge-coloring conjecture; its general resolution is not given here.

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2010). “The case $k=3$ is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem, and the cases $k=4$, which was conjectured by Seymour, and $k=5$ were proved by Guenin.”

record.title: Generalized S-genus identity for ternary quadratic forms over totally real fields
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a totally real number field of class number one in which $2$ is inert, and let $A_F$ be its ring of integers. Suppose that $2S(A_F^\times)^2$ is the squarefree determinant squareclass of a totally positive definite $A_F$-valued binary quadratic form, and that $W\bmod A_F$ divides $S$. For a ternary quadratic form $Q$, define

$$
\epsilon_W(Q):=\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\mid W}\varepsilon_{\mathfrak{p}}(\operatorname{Gen}(Q)).
$$

Let $r_Q(m)$ denote the representation number and $\operatorname{Aut}(Q)$ the automorphism group. **Generalized S-genus identity.** There is a constant $\kappa_F\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ depending only on $F$ such that, for every totally positive $m\in A_F$ satisfying $W\mid m$ and $m\in(A_F^\times)^2\cup 2(A_F^\times)^2\pmod{4A_F}$,

$$
\sum_{Q\in\text{$S$-genus}}\epsilon_W(Q)\frac{r_Q(m)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(Q)|}=\kappa_F W^{[F:\mathbb{Q}]}\frac{r_{x^2+y^2+z^2}(m/W^2)}{|\operatorname{Aut}(x^2+y^2+z^2)|}.
$$

This proposes a generalization of the proved S-genus identities from the rational setting to totally real number fields satisfying the stated hypotheses. The constant is asserted to depend only on $F$, while the identity is required uniformly for all admissible totally positive $m$.
record.source_name: Alexander Berkovich, Jonathan Hanke and William Jagy, “A proof of the S-genus identities for ternary quadratic forms”, arXiv:1010.1926 (2011).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for bipartite graphs of defect four
record.statement:
Let $D835$ and $D$ be natural numbers with $D835
e 6$, and let $D835^b(D835,D)$ denote the largest order of a bipartite graph of maximum degree $D835$ and diameter $D$. Let $D835^b(D835,D)$ be the Moore bipartite bound, and let a bipartite $(D835,D,-4)$-graph have order $D835^b(D835,D)-4$.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no bipartite $(D835,D,-4)$-graph with $D835
e 3$ and $D\ge 5$.

The paper proves nonexistence when $D\ge5$ is odd and establishes several additional upper bounds, but the conjecture remains open for the remaining parameter values.

record.title: The anisotropic Calderón conjecture for Riemannian manifolds
record.statement:
Let $(M,g_1)$ and $(M,g_2)$ be two compact oriented Riemannian manifolds with smooth boundary and dimension $n\geq 3$. For a metric $g$, let

$$
C_g=\{(u|_{\partial M},\partial_{\nu}u|_{\partial M});\,\Delta_g u=0\text{ in }M,\ u\in C^{\infty}(M)\}
$$

be the Cauchy data set of harmonic functions. **The anisotropic Calderón conjecture.** If $C_{g_1}=C_{g_2}$, then

$$
g_2=\psi^*g_1
$$

for some diffeomorphism $\psi:M\to M$ satisfying $\psi|_{\partial M}=\operatorname{Id}$. This is the geometric formulation of Calderón's inverse problem: boundary measurements determine the Riemannian metric up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary. The supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture was resolved, so its status is left open.
record.source_name: Tony Liimatainen and Mikko Salo, “Nowhere conformally homogeneous manifolds and limiting Carleman weights”, arXiv:1011.2507 (2010).

record.title: The six-color conjecture for star chromatic index of subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a **subcubic graph**, meaning a graph of maximum degree at most $3$, and let $chi_{\rm s}'(G)$ denote its star chromatic index, the minimum number of colors in a star edge-coloring of $G$.

**Six-color conjecture.** If $G$ is a subcubic graph, then

$$
\chi_{\rm s}'(G)\le 6.
$$

The paper has already established the bound $\chi_{\rm s}'(G)\le 7$ for subcubic graphs and gives $\chi_{\rm s}'(K_{3,3})=6$, while noting that the Heawood graph also has star chromatic index at most $6$. The proposed improvement from seven to six colors remains open in the supplied source context.

record.title: The local-field fewnomial root-count conjecture
record.statement:
Let $
Omega_L(n,k)$ denote the maximum number of non-degenerate roots in a local field $L$ of a system of $n$ polynomials in $n$ variables having at most $k$ monomials in total. There are absolute constants $C_2>C_1>0$ such that, for any local field $L$ of characteristic $0$ and any $n,k\geq 2$, 

$$
(n+k-1)^{C_1\min\{n,k-1\}}\leq\Omega_L(n,k)\leq(n+k-1)^{C_2\min\{n,k-1\}}.
$$

This conjecture predicts matching polynomial-order bounds for fewnomial systems over all characteristic-zero local fields; the preceding discussion gives substantially different known bounds in Archimedean and non-Archimedean settings, while the proposed uniform estimates remain open.

record.title: Fine's existence conjecture for the extended g-vector
record.statement: Let $X$ be a convex polytope, and let the extended $g$-vector be the vector whose components are the linear functions on flag vectors specified by the axioms in the previous section. **Fine's existence conjecture.** There is a $g$-vector that satisfies the stated axioms. This is the first of two conjectures intended to determine the extended $g$-vector in each dimension; together with the finite-calculation conjecture, it would yield linear inequalities on convex-polytope flag vectors.

record.title: Pfaffian evaluations for Motzkin, Delannoy, Schröder and Narayana sequences
record.statement:
Let $M_n=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom{n}{2k}C_k$ be the Motzkin numbers, $D_n=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom{n}{k}\binom{n+k}{k}$ the central Delannoy numbers, $S_n=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom{n+k}{2k}C_k$ the Schröder numbers, and $N_n(a)=\sum_{k=0}^n\frac1n\binom{n}{k}\binom{n}{k-1}a^k$ the Narayana polynomials, with $N_0(a)=1$. **Motzkin–Delannoy–Schröder–Narayana Pfaffian conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq1$,

$$
\mathop{\rm Pf}\biggl((j-i)M_{i+j-3}\biggr)_{1\leq i,j\leq 2n}=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(4k+1),
$$

$$
\mathop{\rm Pf}\biggl((j-i)D_{i+j-3}\biggr)_{1\leq i,j\leq 2n}=2^{n^2-1}(2n-1)\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}(4k-1),
$$

$$
\mathop{\rm Pf}\biggl((j-i)S_{i+j-2}\biggr)_{1\leq i,j\leq 2n}=2^{n^2}\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(4k+1),
$$

 and

$$
\mathop{\rm Pf}\biggl((j-i)N_{i+j-2}(a)\biggr)_{1\leq i,j\leq 2n}=a^{n^2}\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(4k+1).
$$

These are conjectural Pfaffian evaluations based on lattice-path sequences and computer experiments. Since $C_n=N_n(1)$, $S_n=N_n(2)$, and the stated relation expresses $M_{n-1}$ through $N_n$, proving the Narayana identity would imply the Motzkin and Schröder identities; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Masao Ishikawa, Hiroyuki Tagawa and Jiang Zeng, “Pfaffian decomposition and a Pfaffian analogue of q-Catalan Hankel determinants”, arXiv:1011.5941 (2010).

record.title: The semi-orthogonal decomposition conjecture for gaps in Orlov spectra
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth algebraic variety, and let

$$
\left\langle \mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_n\right\rangle
$$

be a semi-orthogonal decomposition of $\operatorname{D}^{\operatorname{b}}(\operatorname{coh} X)$. A **gap conjecture for semi-orthogonal decompositions.** The length of any gap in the spectrum of $\operatorname{D}^{\operatorname{b}}(\operatorname{coh} X)$ is at most the minimum of the maximal Rouquier dimension amongst the $\mathcal A_i$ and the maximal gap amongst the $\mathcal A_i$. This is proposed after a theorem giving an upper bound on gaps from generators of semi-orthogonal components; the conjecture remains purely conjectural in the source.

record.title: The edge-connectivity conjecture for UBB cardinality
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\lambda(G)$ denote its edge connectivity, meaning the minimum number of edges whose removal disconnects $G$. For an integer $t$, a **$t$-UBB** is an uncovering-by-bases structure with parameter $t$, and its cardinality is its number of spanning trees.

**Edge-connectivity UBB conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda(G)=k,
$$

then there exists a $(k-1)$-UBB for $G$ with cardinality

$$
|E(G)|.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the constructions discussed in the source, where the number of spanning trees in the $t$-UBB is bounded above by the number of edges. The source describes this as possibly optimistic and does not report a resolution.

record.title: Barat–Füredi–Kantor–Kim–Patkos conjecture on a-union-free subfamilies
record.statement:
Let $a\geq 2$ be an integer. A family of sets is **$a$-union-free** if it has no $a+1$ distinct sets $X_1,\ldots,X_{a+1}$ such that $X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_a=X_{a+1}$. Let $g(m,a)$ be the minimum, over all families of $m$ sets, of the size of the largest $a$-union-free subfamily.

**Barat–Füredi–Kantor–Kim–Patkos conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty}\liminf_{m\rightarrow\infty}\frac{g(m,a)}{\sqrt{m}}=\infty.
$$

The abstract says that the paper verifies this conjecture in a strong form, so it is solved.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox, Choongbum Lee and Benny Sudakov, “Maximum union-free subfamilies”, arXiv:1012.3127 (2011).

record.title: The Boolean-algebra subfamily extremal conjecture
record.statement: Let $m=2^n$, and consider families of $m$ sets. A subfamily forms a Boolean algebra of dimension $d$ if it is isomorphic to the Boolean lattice $2^{[d]}$. **Boolean-algebra subfamily extremal conjecture.** The family containing the largest number of subfamilies forming a Boolean algebra of dimension $d$ is $2^{[n]}$. This proposes that the full Boolean lattice is extremal for the number of $d$-dimensional Boolean-algebra subfamilies among families of $2^n$ sets; the source gives no resolution status or further conditions.

record.title: The strong-duality polynomial-solvability conjecture for optimization problems
record.statement: Let $P_a$ and $P_b$ be optimization problems such that one is the dual of the other, so that they exhibit strong duality. **Strong-duality polynomial-solvability conjecture.** Both $P_a$ and $P_b$ should be polynomially solvable. This conjecture is motivated by the canonical dual examples discussed in the paper, where strong duality and polynomial-time solution coexist; its general validity is not established here.

record.title: The constant-term conjecture for W-algebra extensions of (2,p) minimal models
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers. For a Laurent series in $x_1,\ldots,x_{2k+1}$, write ${\rm CT}_{x_1,\ldots,x_{2k+1}}$ for its constant term, and let $r!!$ denote the double factorial. Then, up to a sign,

$$
{\rm CT}_{x_1,\ldots,x_{2k+1}} \frac{1}{(x_1 \cdots x_{2k+1})^{(2m+1)k}} \prod_{i=1}^k {\rm ln}\left(1-\frac{x_{2i}}{x_{2i-1}}\right) \prod_{1 \leq i <j \leq 2k+1 }(x_i-x_j)^{2m+1}
$$

**Constant-term conjecture.** This constant term equals

$$
\frac{((2k+1)(2m+1))!!}{(2k+1)!!(2m+1)!!^{2k+1}}.
$$

The conjecture would determine the nonzero constant left unspecified in the preceding corollary and is presented as an analogue of a conjecture from the cited earlier work; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The supercohomology determination conjecture
record.statement: Let supercohomology be the cohomological invariant under consideration, let the Jacobian ring encode the relevant algebraic data, let gaps refer to gaps in the associated categorical generation spectrum, and let $ME$ denote the monodromy effect. **Supercohomology determination conjecture.** The dimension of supercohomology is determined by the Jacobian ring, gaps, and the monodromy effect $ME$. The conjecture proposes that these algebraic, categorical, and monodromy data determine the size of supercohomology; the supplied text does not state a precise formula or known cases.

record.title: Krivelevich–Yuster conjecture on rainbow connection and minimum degree
record.statement:
All graphs are undirected, finite and simple. For a connected graph $G$, let $n$ be its number of vertices, let $\delta(G)$ be its minimum degree, and let $rc(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of $G$ such that every two distinct vertices are joined by a path whose edges have pairwise distinct colors.

**Krivelevich–Yuster conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq 3,
$$

then

$$
rc(G)<\frac{3n}{4}.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the previously known bound $rc(G)<20n/\delta(G)$ for connected graphs. Its resolution status is not specified in the provided source material.

record.title: Robust decay for higher-dimensional sectionally-hyperbolic singular flows
record.statement: Consider smooth singular flows in dimensions higher than three that are **sectionally-hyperbolic**, meaning that they belong to the higher-dimensional class described in the source, generalizing hyperbolicity for singular flows and including singular-hyperbolic attractors in three-manifolds. **The sectional-hyperbolicity conjecture.** Such flows exhibit robust exponential decay of correlations. The source presents this as a proposed higher-dimensional extension; sectional-hyperbolicity is described as a generalization containing the three-dimensional singular-hyperbolic case, and the claim remains open.

record.title: The effective Bogomolov conjecture for tori and abelian varieties
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a torus or an abelian variety, and let $\hat h$ be a canonical height associated with an ample line bundle on a compactification of $G$.

**Effective Bogomolov conjecture.** There is a real number $c>0$ such that every proper closed irreducible subvariety $X$ of $G$ that is not contained in a translate of a proper algebraic subgroup of $G$ satisfies

$$
\hat\mu(X)\geq c\,(\deg(X))^{-1/\operatorname{codim}(X)}.
$$

This is the expected optimal degree dependence for an effective lower bound on the essential minimum. The source records the bound for tori up to an arbitrarily small loss in the exponent and presents the displayed statement as the natural conjectural extension to abelian, and possibly semi-abelian, varieties.

record.title: Degree condition for maximum-length cycles in bipartite digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a bipartite digraph with colour classes $X$ and $Y$ such that $|X|=a\leq b=|Y|$. For vertices $u$ and $v$ in opposite colour classes with $uv\notin A(D)$, consider the degree condition

$$
d^+(u)+d^-(v)>\frac{a+b+2}{2}.
$$

**Maximum-cycle degree conjecture.** If this inequality holds whenever $u$ and $v$ lie in opposite colour classes and $uv\notin A(D)$, then $D$ contains an oriented cycle of length $2a$.

This is an Ore-type sufficient condition for a bipartite digraph to contain a cycle meeting every vertex of its smaller colour class. The source states that the conjecture is proved in the balanced case $a=b$, while the general case remains open.

record.title: Chakraborty–Fischer–Matsliah–Yuster conjecture on bounded strong rainbow connection
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices, let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree, and let $src(G)$ denote its strong rainbow connection number. For a fixed positive constant $\epsilon$, **Chakraborty–Fischer–Matsliah–Yuster's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq \epsilon n,
$$

then $G$ has bounded strong rainbow connection number. This conjecture concerns the non-monotone strong rainbow connection parameter and predicts a bound independent of the graph size under linear minimum degree.

record.title: The diameter-three conjecture for small Weyl graphs
record.statement: Let $\Phi$ be an irreducible classical root system of rank at least $2$, and let $\Gamma_s(\Phi)$ be its small Weyl graph. The diameter of a graph is the maximum distance between two of its vertices. **Diameter-three conjecture.** The diameter of $\Gamma_s(\Phi)$ is at most $3$. This is suggested by computations for several root systems, in which the diameter was always at most $3$; the general case remains open.
